question.leadin: A certain city's boule oversaw the process for dealing this kind of punishment, which required 6000 votes to be carried out.
question.text: Name this kind of punishment,which was dealt to people who were ostracized in ancient Athens.

swap.leadin: This city was home to figures like Alcibiades (AAL-sib-ee-AH-deez) and Draco.
swap.text: Name this powerful city-state of Ancient Greece. This city organized many other Greek cities into the Delian League after the defeat of the Persian Invasion.
swap.clue: A bema, or speaker's platform, lies on this city's Pnyx hill.

question.leadin: In 336 BCE, this man succeeded his father, Philip II; within two years, he had pacified Greece and started an invasion of Persia.
question.text: Name this "Great" Macedonian leader, whose Hellenistic empire eventually stretched to India before he died at the age of 32.
question.clue: This ruler's defeat of Porus at the Hydaspes led to the annexation of much of Punjab at the cost of their horse Bucephalus.

swap.leadin: Name these Wonders of the Ancient World.
swap.text: This tall bronze statue on the island of Rhodes was not, in fact, tall enough to span the harbor, but few people could link their arms around one of its thumbs.
swap.clue: An Egyptian offer to rebuild this structure was refused after a 226 BCE earthquake destroyed it.

question.text: The Thera eruption didn't wipe out this civilization, but the Mycenaean army obliged. Arthur Evans excavated this civilization's site of Knossos.
question.clue: The Phaistos Disc is a relic of these people, who developed the Linear A script.

swap.text: Xenophon (ZEE-nuh-fahn) credited Lycurgus with introducing this rigorous education and training program, which Spartan boys entered at the age of seven.
swap.clue: The Eurypontids and Agiads were exempted from this system, which moved top performers to the krypteia ("krip-TAI-uh"), where they would terrorize helots ("HELL-uts").

question.text: The destruction of the Long Walls at Aegospotami was led by this Spartan admiral, who clashed with Antiochus at the Battle of Notium. This military leader negotiated with Theramenes after blockading Piraeus.
question.clue: This beneficiary of Cyrus the Younger's patronage resumed his most famous office after his replacement Callicratidas lost the battle of Arginusae.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a war that lasted from 431 to 404 BCE.
swap.text: The war effectively ended for good after this 405 BCE naval defeat of the Athenians. In this battle, the Spartans under Lysander cut off Athens from the Black Sea's grain exports, causing disaster and famine in the city.
swap.clue: A plan to move the fleet up to Sertos suggested to the losing commanders by Alcibiades was rejected.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Ionian city of Halicarnassus.
question.text: Among the famous rulers of the city of Halicarnassus was Artemisia I, a client queen and trusted war councillor of the Persian Xerxes I who fought extremely well at this Persian naval defeat by Themistocles the Athenian in 480 BCE.
question.clue: This battle took place following one side's retreat at Artemisium.

swap.text: An 1840 blood libel occurred on this Ottoman-ruled island. Philippe Villiers de L'Isle-Adam ("fee-LEEP veel-YAY duh LEEL ah-DOM") and 600 Knights Hospitaller ("hoss-PIT-ah-lur") defended this island for six months in 1522.
swap.clue: Previously this polity had been a powerful federal state dominating the commercial traffic of the Eastern Mediterranean through its five ports.

question.leadin: Name these participants in acts of mass slaughter.
question.text: In 415 BC, Athens killed all the men of this neutral island city-state. Thucydides composed a noted debate in which the Athenians try to talk the city into surrendering.
question.clue: This island was involved in a diplomatic dispute immediately after the first battle of Mantinea, whose resolution likely inspired Euripides to write The Trojan Women.

swap.leadin: Name these following about a race described in Greek myth.
swap.text: One of Heracles' labors was to retrieve the girdle worn by this queen.

question.text: Donald Kagan said that the surrender at Sphacteria "shook the world" in a history of this conflict. Thucydides also documented this conflict.
question.clue: It briefly halted during the Peace of Nicias, which broke for the failed Sicilian expedition under Alcibiades.

swap.leadin: After he was tried for failing to capture this city, one monarch explained that because he had really captured a nearby forest of the same name, he had fulfilled an oracle's prophecy.
swap.text: Name this city that was the origin and namesake of the Macedonian royal family. This city engaged in the Battle of the Champions with its longtime rival, Sparta.
swap.clue: Weights and measures found at the Heraion of this city are said to date to the reign of King Pheidon, who ruled this city as a tyrant.

question.text: Chandragupta Maurya defeated an invasion by one of these people who fought at the Battles of Corupedium and Ipsus. They included Demetrius I and Lysimachus.
question.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

swap.text: This tyrant of Samos was noted by Herodotus for building three great structures - the great Heraion temple, a great mole in the harbour, and a kilometre long underground aqueduct impressively started from both ends at the same time.
swap.clue: This ruler patronized the poets Ibycus (IH-bih-kus) and Anacreon (uh-NAH-kree-on), possibly using money gained through rampant piracy, such as when his fleet of 100 penteconters raided Miletus (my-LEE-tus) and Lesbos.

question.text: The Panhellenic colony of Thurii (thoo-ree-"eye") was established at the direction of Pericles in this larger region. This term refers to colonies like Croton and Sybaris that first brought Greek culture to southern Italy and Sicily.
question.clue: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in a city in this region.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the situation in the Greek world just before the rise of Macedon.
swap.text: In this 371 battle, Epaminondas led the Thebans to victory over Cleombrotus and Sparta, beginning the brief pre-eminence of Thebes before the arrival of Philip.
swap.clue: The Theban Sacred Band under Epaminondas won a stunning victory against the Spartan phalanx at this 371 BC battle.

question.leadin: The second ruler of this name commissioned the ship Syracusia.
question.text: Give this name of two rulers of Syracuse, the first of whom defeated the Etruscans at the Battle of Cumae, and the second of whom patronised Archimedes.

swap.text: This Corinthian ruler was a member of the Seven Sages and created a ship's' dragway between the Saronic and Corinthian Gulfs called the Diolkos. The Corcyrans, who didn't want his rule, killed his son Lycophron to prevent them from swapping thrones.
swap.clue: This man sent three hundred Corcyran nobles to Alyattes, ruler of Lydia, to be made eunuchs.
